newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania and Ukraine sign historic treaty.
newsitem.headline: Romania and Ukraine sign historic treaty.

text.p: Romania and Ukraine signed on Monday a long-delayed political treaty expected to settle thorny post-World War Two differences over borders and help Romania bolster its prospects for fast-track NATO membership.

The treaty caps three years of efforts by the two neighbours to put behind them issues left over from a pact signed nearly 60 years ago between Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union, under which Romania lost territories to Moscow.
Romanian President Emil Constantinescu signed the treaty with his Ukrainian counterpart Leonid Kuchma in the Black Sea resort of Neptun, 250 km (160 miles) east of Bucharest.
Kuchma was greeted with military honours when he arrived at the signing ceremony, which took place at the former summer residence of late Stalinist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu.

The treaty will dampen arguments related to land lost by Romania under the 1939 Soviet-Nazi pact, but differences remain over borders I n the Black Sea area, which both sides beliueve to be rich in oil and gas.
Under the 1939 Soviet-Nazi pact, Moscow annexed Romania's lands of Bukovina, southern Bessarabia and the Serpent Island, now in Ukraine.
